# 12-Week Programme: 34F, Stage III Endometriosis

**Start:** Monday 1 June 2026 · **End:** Sunday 23 August 2026

---

## Before You Start

**Medical clearance.** Stage III endometriosis often involves adhesions and endometriomas. Get sign-off from her gynaecologist. A pelvic floor physiotherapy assessment is also strongly recommended, because hypertonic pelvic floor is common with endo and affects how she should brace.

**Projected cycle dates.** These come from her last period (4 May 2026), a 27-day cycle, and 4 flow days. Cycles drift, so confirm with her each week and shift the restricted days as needed.

| Cycle | Projected flow days |
|---|---|
| 1 | Sun 31 May – Wed 3 Jun (programme overlap: Mon 1 – Wed 3 Jun) |
| 2 | Sat 27 Jun – Tue 30 Jun |
| 3 | Fri 24 Jul – Mon 27 Jul |
| 4 | Thu 20 Aug – Sun 23 Aug |

**Reported flare windows:** Fri 10 – Mon 13 Jul, and Tue 4 – Fri 7 Aug.

**Restricted days.** On every flow and flare day there is no HIIT, no heavy Valsalva (no near-max lifts or breath-held bracing), and no jumping or plyometrics. On these days, replace the planned session with the **Gentle Session (G)** below, or rest if symptoms are severe. Pain overrides the plan, always.

---

## Weekly Template (unrestricted weeks)

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Strength A (lower-body emphasis) |
| Tue | Zone 2 cardio, 30–45 min |
| Wed | Mobility + core (pelvic-floor-friendly) |
| Thu | Strength B (upper-body + posterior chain) |
| Fri | Conditioning (intervals; HIIT from Phase 2) |
| Sat | Long low-intensity: walk, hike, or swim, 45–60 min |
| Sun | Rest |

### Gentle Session (G), for restricted days, 20–40 min
- 10–20 min easy walk or cycle at RPE 3–4
- Diaphragmatic breathing in supported child's pose or 90/90 position, 5 min
- Cat-cow, open book, supported hip-flexor stretch, figure-4, and happy baby, 2 × 45 s each
- Optional light work, exhaling on effort with no breath-holding: glute bridge 2×12, banded row 2×15, dead bug 2×8/side
- Heat pack afterwards if it helps

---

## Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4, 1–28 June)

**Goals:** movement quality, exhale-on-effort breathing, aerobic base. Work at RPE 6–7 and leave 3+ reps in reserve.

**Strength A:** Goblet squat 3×10 · DB Romanian deadlift 3×10 · Split squat 3×8/side · Glute bridge 3×12 · Pallof press 3×10/side

**Strength B:** DB bench or incline press 3×10 · 1-arm row 3×10/side · Lat pulldown 3×10 · Hip hinge (KB deadlift) 3×10 · Side plank 3×20 s/side

**Friday Conditioning:** Steady tempo work only, e.g. bike 6 × 1 min at RPE 7 with 2 min easy. No jumping in this phase.

**Week-by-week**
- **W1 (1–7 Jun):** Mon–Wed are flow days, so Mon = G, Tue = G or easy walk, Wed = mobility. Thu = Strength B, Fri = conditioning, Sat = long walk. Use light loads to learn patterns.
- **W2 (8–14 Jun):** Full template.
- **W3 (15–21 Jun):** Full template with +1 set on the main lifts.
- **W4 (22–28 Jun):** Deload. Run the full template at about 70% volume. **Sat 27 and Sun 28 are flow days:** Sat = G, Sun = rest.

---

## Phase 2: Build (Weeks 5–8, 29 June – 26 July)

**Goals:** progressive load, introduce intervals and low-level plyometrics on unrestricted days. Work at RPE 7–8 in sets of 6–10 reps.

**Strength A:** Back squat or safety-bar squat 4×6–8 · RDL 3×8 · Reverse lunge 3×8/side · Hip thrust 3×10 · Low box step-downs 3×8 · Suitcase carry 3×30 m

**Strength B:** Bench press 4×6–8 · Chest-supported row 4×8 · Assisted pull-up 3×6–8 · Trap-bar deadlift 3×6 · Half-kneeling landmine press 3×8/side

**Friday HIIT:** Bike or rower, 8 × 30 s hard / 90 s easy. Add 2×5 low pogo hops at the end, only if she is pelvic-floor cleared and symptom-free.

**Week-by-week**
- **W5 (29 Jun – 5 Jul):** **Mon 29 and Tue 30 are flow days:** Mon = G, Tue = easy walk. Wed = mobility, Thu = Strength B, Fri = HIIT, Sat = long, Sun = rest. Fit Strength A in on Wed if she feels good, otherwise skip it this week.

# Nutrition Plan: Anti-Inflammatory Eating to Support the Programme

Use this alongside the training plan. It stays within general healthy-eating guidance, which is within a trainer's scope in most regions. **Refer her to a registered dietitian** for elimination diets, supplements, or if she has significant GI symptoms, a history of disordered eating, or is trying to conceive.

**What the evidence supports:** Dietary approaches to endometriosis have limited research. Most studies are small or observational. A Mediterranean-style pattern rich in omega-3, fibre, and plants is associated with lower inflammation and better symptom reports in some studies, and it supports training and recovery. Present it as "may help, low risk, good for performance," not as a treatment.

---

## 1. Core Principles

| Principle | Target | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Mediterranean-style base** | Most meals built on vegetables, legumes, whole grains, olive oil, fish | Best-supported anti-inflammatory pattern overall |
| **Protein** | About 1.6 g/kg/day, split over 3–4 meals (~25–35 g each) | Supports strength gains and recovery |
| **Omega-3 fats** | Oily fish 2–3×/week (salmon, sardines, mackerel, trout), plus walnuts, chia, flax | Some evidence of reduced inflammation and pain |
| **Fibre** | 25–30 g/day, increased gradually | Gut health and oestrogen clearance; lower if bloating flares |
| **Colourful plants** | 5+ portions/day, including cruciferous veg (broccoli, cabbage, kale) and berries | Antioxidants and polyphenols |
| **Extra-virgin olive oil** | Main cooking and dressing fat | Anti-inflammatory polyphenols |
| **Hydration** | About 2–2.5 L/day, more on training days | Performance, digestion, cramping |

**Reduce, without banning:**
- **Processed and red meat.** Higher intake is associated with endo risk in observational data. Keep red meat to about 1–2×/week and processed meat occasional.
- **Ultra-processed foods and added sugar.**
- **Alcohol.** Keep it low, and avoid it especially around flow and flare windows.
- **Caffeine.** Moderate, up to about 2–3 cups of coffee daily. Cut back if she notices it worsens pain or sleep.

Frame these as "more of" and "less often," not as forbidden foods. Rigid restriction backfires and can worsen stress, which she reports as a flare trigger.

---

## 2. Calculating Her Targets

You'll need her body weight. Example for a 65 kg client:

- **Protein:** 65 × 1.6 = **~105 g/day**, or about 4 meals of 25–30 g
- **Energy:** Don't run an aggressive deficit during this programme. Maintenance or a very mild deficit supports recovery and hormonal health. If body composition is a goal, keep any deficit modest (~300 kcal/day) and only with dietitian input.
- **Carbohydrate:** Higher on Strength and HIIT days, moderate on rest and G days.

---

## 3. Sample Day (Training Day, ~65 kg Client)

**Breakfast:** Overnight oats with Greek yoghurt, chia seeds, berries, and walnuts *(~30 g protein)*

**Lunch:** Large salad with quinoa or lentils, roast vegetables, leafy greens, a tinned sardine or chicken portion, and olive oil–lemon dressing *(~30 g)*

**Pre-training snack (60–90 min before):** Banana with a small handful of almonds, or toast with nut butter

**Post-training / dinner:** Baked salmon, roasted sweet potato, steamed broccoli, tahini drizzle *(~35 g)*

**Evening (optional):** Kefir or yoghurt with ground flax, or a small handful of dark chocolate and nuts *(~10–15 g)*

---

## 4. Weekly Structure

| Day | Training | Nutrition focus |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Strength A | Carbs around the session; protein at every meal |
| Tue | Zone 2 | Moderate carbs; oily fish dinner |
| Wed | Mobility + core | Legume-based meals (lentil soup, chickpea curry) |
| Thu | Strength B | Carbs around the session; oily fish or poultry |
| Fri | Conditioning / HIIT | Carbs before the session; recovery meal within ~2 h |
| Sat | Long low-intensity | Hydrate well; bring a snack for 60+ min sessions |
| Sun | Rest | Batch cook for the week (grains, roast veg, legumes, sauces) |

**Batch-cook staples:** quinoa or brown rice, roasted vegetable trays, a pot of lentil or bean soup, baked salmon or chicken portions, jars of olive oil–lemon dressing.

---

## 5. Cycle and Flare Adjustments

Use the same dates as the training plan.

### Flow days
(1–3 Jun, 27–30 Jun, 24–27 Jul, 20–23 Aug)
- **Iron:** Prioritise iron-rich foods such as lean red meat (a good use of the weekly allowance), lentils, spinach, tofu, and fortified cereals. Pair them with vitamin C (peppers, citrus, berries). Keep tea and coffee away from iron-rich meals.
- **Warm, easy-to-digest meals** such as soups, stews, and porridge.
- **Magnesium-rich foods** may help cramping: leafy greens, pumpkin seeds, dark chocolate, legumes.
- **Fluids:** keep them up. A heat pack plus warm drinks like ginger tea often helps.

### Flare days
(10–13 Jul, 4–7 Aug, plus any unplanned flares)
- **Lower energy needs** on G or rest days, but don't skip meals. Under-eating worsens fatigue.
- **If bloating or GI pain is present:** temporarily reduce high-fibre and gas-forming foods (raw cruciferous veg, beans, onion, garlic). Switch to cooked veg, rice, oats, eggs, fish, and yoghurt, then return to normal as symptoms settle.
- **Ginger** (tea or fresh in cooking) may ease nausea and discomfort.
- **Avoid alcohol** and keep caffeine lower.
- **Small, frequent meals** rather than large ones.

### Luteal phase
(Roughly the 7–10 days before each flow)
- Appetite often rises. Allow a slightly larger intake with extra complex carbs and protein rather than fighting it.
- Ease up on salt if she notices bloating.

---

## 6. Supplements: Refer, Don't Prescribe

Several supplements have some research in endometriosis or general inflammation, including omega-3 fish oil, vitamin D, magnesium, and iron if levels are low. **Do not recommend doses.** Suggest she ask her GP or gynaecologist to check **ferritin, vitamin D, and B12**, and discuss any supplements with them or a dietitian. Some can interact with hormonal treatments she may be on.

---

## 7. Tracking

Add these to her daily symptom log:
- Rough meal pattern (a photo log is easiest)
- Bloating and bowel symptoms (0–10)
- Alcohol and caffeine
- Any foods she suspects trigger symptoms

After 4–6 weeks, review this with her. **If she sees clear patterns, such as consistent bloating after certain foods, refer her to a dietitian** to explore something structured like low-FODMAP, rather than cutting foods herself.

---

## 8. Red Flags: Refer Promptly

- Rapid weight loss, fear of foods, or increasingly restrictive eating
- Persistent GI symptoms (pain, diarrhoea, constipation, blood)
- Fatigue or breathlessness suggesting anaemia, which is common with heavy flow
- Missed or significantly changed periods

# Cardio Plan: Building Her Aerobic Base

This replaces the loose "Zone 2, 30–45 min" and "Long low-intensity" slots in the original template with a progressive, dated plan. Friday conditioning and HIIT stay as written. This plan covers the **easy aerobic work**, which is where base is built.

---

## 1. Why Mostly Easy Cardio

Aerobic base comes mainly from **volume at low intensity**, not from hard sessions. Easy cardio also suits her well:

- **It fits around strength work.** Low-intensity cardio interferes very little with strength gains, so it won't undercut Phases 2–3.
- **It is allowed on restricted days.** Her flow and flare restrictions rule out HIIT, heavy Valsalva, and jumping, not easy movement. Gentle aerobic work can be kept on many restricted days if she feels up to it, and some people find it eases cramping.
- **It is low risk** for stress and symptom flares compared with high-intensity work.

**Target split:** about 80–90% of her weekly cardio time easy, and 10–20% hard (the Friday sessions only).

---

## 2. Intensity: How to Find "Easy"

Use more than one method, because heart rate varies across the cycle. It often runs a few beats higher in the luteal phase, and higher again during flares or poor sleep.

| Method | Zone 2 / easy target |
|---|---|
| **Talk test** (primary) | Can speak in full sentences; nose breathing possible most of the time |
| **RPE** | 3–4 out of 10 |
| **Heart rate** (guide only) | About 60–70% of max. The age estimate (220 − 34 ≈ 186 bpm) gives roughly **112–130 bpm**. Age formulas can be off by 10+ bpm, so let the talk test overrule them. |

If her heart rate drifts high at her usual pace in the luteal phase or on a bad day, **slow down to stay at the same effort.** Don't chase pace.

---

## 3. Modality Choices

**Preferred, low-impact:** incline treadmill walk, elliptical, rower, swimming, and outdoor walking or hiking.

**Cycling:** good, but saddle pressure can aggravate pelvic pain for some women with endo. Offer a recumbent bike, a wider or cut-out saddle, or a standing/rower alternative if she reports discomfort.

**Running:** fine on unrestricted days **if her pelvic floor assessment clears it** and it doesn't provoke symptoms. Use walk–run intervals if she's new to it. **On flow and flare days, use low-impact options only.** Running isn't jumping, but repeated impact is a sensible thing to avoid on those days.

**Restricted-day cardio rules:**
- Easy only, at RPE ≤ 4
- Keep it to 15–30 minutes, inside or in place of the Gentle Session (G)
- Low-impact modalities only
- Stop or shorten if pain rises during or after. Rest is always a valid choice.

---

## 4. Updated Weekly Template (Unrestricted Weeks)

| Day | Session | Cardio |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Strength A | none |
| Tue | **Zone 2 (main)** | 30 → 50 min |
| Wed | Mobility + core | **Zone 2 add-on**, 20 → 30 min, before mobility |
| Thu | Strength B | **Optional 15–20 min easy** cool-down from Phase 2 onward |
| Fri | Conditioning / HIIT | as in the training plan |

**Progression rule:** increase weekly easy minutes by no more than about 10–15% per week. Weeks with flow or flare days **hold or drop** volume rather than trying to catch up. Never stack missed minutes onto the following days.

---

## 5. Baseline and Retest

Use a **fixed-effort aerobic test** to measure base. A max test would be inappropriate here and isn't needed.

**Protocol:** 10 min easy warm-up, then **20 min at a steady heart rate about 125 bpm** (or the top of her talk-test zone), on the same machine each time. Record the **distance or average watts** covered.

- **Baseline:** Sat 6 June (Week 1, first unrestricted Saturday, after the flow days)
- **Retest:** Tue 18 August (Week 12, before the projected flow on 20 August)

A better result at the same heart rate means her aerobic base has improved. Note her cycle day on both tests. If the retest falls in a different phase, interpret small differences cautiously.

# Phase 2 Revision: Higher Intensity (Weeks 5–8, 29 June – 26 July)

This replaces the Phase 2 section of the training plan and updates the Phase 2 rows of the cardio plan. Phases 1 and 3, the nutrition plan, and all restricted-day rules stay the same.

---

## 1. What Changes and What Doesn't

**Increasing:**
- **Strength load and effort.** RPE rises from 7–8 to 8–8.5, with top sets of 5–6 reps by Week 8.
- **Interval intensity.** Intervals get longer and harder, and lost Friday HIIT sessions are moved to another day rather than dropped.
- **Density.** Accessory work moves into supersets with shorter rests.

**Unchanged:**
- **No HIIT, heavy Valsalva, or jumping on flow or flare days.** Phase 2 contains 6 restricted days: 29–30 Jun, 10–13 Jul, and 24–26 Jul.
- **About 80% of cardio time stays easy.** Pushing intensity means harder hard sessions, not more of them.
- **Exhale-on-effort bracing on all days.** She should exhale through the hardest part of each rep rather than holding her breath. Breath-holding raises intra-abdominal pressure, which is the main pelvic concern for her.
- **A 1–2 rep reserve on main lifts.** She should not train to failure. Failure reps are where bracing breaks down and where the injury and flare risk sits.

**Prerequisites for this phase:** gynaecologist clearance, and pelvic floor physio clearance for impact and heavier loading. Phase 1 should also have gone well, with no exercise-provoked pain increases. If she isn't cleared for impact, remove the plyometrics and keep everything else.

## 2. Readiness Check (Before Every Hard Session)

Hard sessions are Strength A, Strength B, and intervals. Run a 30-second check before each one:

| Check | Go | Downgrade |
|---|---|---|
| Pelvic pain today (0–10) | ≤ 3 | 4–5: drop to RPE 7, no intervals. 6+: Gentle Session (G) |
| Sleep last night | Normal | Under 6 h: drop one set from each main lift |
| Resting heart rate | Within ~5 bpm of normal | Up 5–7+ bpm for 2+ days: replace intervals with Zone 2 |
| Early flare signs (bloating, back ache, her personal warning signs) | None | Treat the day as restricted |

Higher intensity is only worth it when she can recover from it. The check keeps the extra push from tipping her into an unplanned flare.

# Adding a Metabolic Conditioning (MetCon) Day

This adds a dedicated MetCon session to the programme. The Friday interval sessions stay. MetCon is a separate session type: circuit-style work using several movements at moderate loads, where Friday is pure intervals on a single machine.

---

## 1. The Constraint

The week already has two strength sessions, one interval session, and a long easy session. A second HIIT-type day is reasonable for her, but only under these rules:

- **Never on flow or flare days.** No exceptions.
- **No more than 2 HIIT-type sessions per week** (MetCon plus intervals).
- **No MetCon the day before a predicted flow or flare day.** Late-luteal and pre-flare recovery is often poor.
- **Never in the first session back after a flare.**
- **About 80% of cardio time stays easy.**

Applying these honestly means **the extra day only fits in weeks without restricted days**: Weeks 2, 3, 4, and 11. In weeks with flow or flare days, there is only room for one hard conditioning session. In those weeks, **MetCon alternates with intervals** rather than being stacked on top, so she still gets regular metabolic work without adding a third hard day in a row. The option to keep intervals instead is covered in Section 6.

# Adding a Plyometric Day

This adds a short, dedicated plyometric session to the programme. To avoid doubling her impact exposure, **all plyometrics now live on this day.** The plyo blocks previously attached to Friday intervals (Phase 2) and Friday HIIT (Phase 3) are removed, and Friday becomes pure intervals. ## 1. Rules

Plyometrics are the highest-impact element in the programme, so they carry the strictest rules.

- **Never on flow or flare days.** Her restriction rules out jumping on those days.
- **Never the day before a predicted flow or flare day.**
- **Never the first session back after flow or a flare.** Landing mechanics are often worse when she is still recovering.
- **Pelvic floor physio clearance for impact is required.** Without it, run the Phase 1 landing-prep session throughout and use the med-ball power options in place of jumps.
- **Low volume, full recovery.** Plyos train power and landing skill, not fitness. Work stays crisp, with 60–90 s between sets.
- **Exhale on take-off and landing.** No breath-holding.
- **Stop immediately** with any leaking, pelvic heaviness, or pelvic pain. Regress to the previous week's level next session and flag it to her physio.
- **The readiness check applies.** If pain is above 3, skip the plyos and do Zone 2 only.

**Never used:** depth or drop jumps, boxes above about 30 cm, jumping *down* from boxes (she steps down), tuck jumps, repeated maximal bounding, or burpees.

# 1RM Testing at the End of Phase 3

**Short answer: I'd recommend an estimated 1RM rather than a true max for this block.** She can still finish with a solid strength number. The test just needs to fit the rules the programme is built on.

---

## 1. Why Not a True 1RM

**Breath-holding.** A genuine max single almost always needs a full Valsalva (breath held against a closed airway) to stay braced. Her restriction bans heavy Valsalva on flow and flare days. Phase 3 also uses exhale-on-effort bracing on *all* days to manage pelvic pressure. A true 1RM would be the single highest intra-abdominal pressure event of the programme, and it is the effort most likely to cause leaking, heaviness, or a pain spike.

**Timing.** End of Phase 3 is Week 12 (17–23 Aug). Her flow is projected from **Thu 20 Aug**, so:
- **Wed 19** is the day before flow. The programme already caps effort then, and late-luteal recovery and pain tolerance are often worse.
- **Thu 20 – Sun 23** are flow days, where heavy Valsalva is off-limits.
- This leaves **Mon 17 and Tue 18** as the only suitable test days, and Tue 18 already holds the aerobic retest.

**Limited payoff.** This is her first structured block. An estimated 1RM tracks progress just as well and carries far less risk.

---

## 2. Recommended Protocol: Estimated 1RM

Test a **heavy set of 3–5 reps at RPE 8–9** with exhale bracing. She should stop with 1–2 reps in reserve. Then calculate:

> **Estimated 1RM = load × (1 + reps ÷ 30)**
> Example: 60 kg × 4 reps → 60 × 1.13 ≈ **68 kg**

**Warm-up per lift:** empty bar ×10, then about 50% ×5, 70% ×3, and 85% ×1, before one test set. Allow 3–4 minutes of rest before the test set. If the test set is clean and well under RPE 8, she may take **one** more attempt at +2.5–5 kg. No more than two test sets per lift.

**A set doesn't count if** she has to hold her breath to finish it, her form breaks down, or she gets any pelvic symptoms. In that case, use the last clean set.

## 4. Conditions for Testing at All

Test only if **all** of these are true. Otherwise, use the W11 working sets as her end-of-block numbers.

## 5. If She Wants a True 1RM in Future

A true max can be reasonable later, under these conditions:
- Her pelvic floor physio **specifically clears breath-hold bracing** for maximal lifts, ideally after assessing her during a heavy lift.
- The test falls on an unrestricted day, well away from flow and flare windows. The mid-follicular phase, roughly days 6–10 of her cycle, is a sensible target.
- She has had a dedicated peaking block with heavy singles at RPE 8–9 beforehand, not just the end of a mixed programme.
- An experienced spotter or safety bars are in place, and attempts stop the moment she reports any pelvic symptom.

I'd plan this for her next block if strength becomes a main goal. For now, the e1RM will give you a reliable baseline to programme from.

## B8. Estimated 1RM Test (W12)

**No true 1RM this block.** A max single requires a breath-held Valsalva, which conflicts with the exhale-bracing rule. The only safe test window before flow is also very narrow.

- **Warm-up:** bar ×10, ~50% ×5, ~70% ×3, ~85% ×1, then rest 3–4 min.
- **Test set:** 3–5 reps at RPE 8–9 with exhale bracing. If the set is clean and well under RPE 8, she may take one more set at +2.5–5 kg. Maximum two test sets per lift.
- **Formula:** e1RM = load × (1 + reps ÷ 30). For example, 60 kg × 4 ≈ 68 kg.
- **Set is void** if she breath-holds, her form breaks, or she has any pelvic symptom. Use the last clean set instead.
- **Trap-bar deadlift:** calculate from W11 Thursday's heaviest clean set. Don't test it in W12.
- **Pull-up:** use max reps at her current assistance, or a weighted 5RM, in W11.
- **Test only if:** she passes the readiness check, the W10 flare has settled, W11 went normally, and her cycle dates are confirmed. Otherwise, use her W11 working sets as end-of-block numbers.

# PART E: Nutrition

**Scope:** General healthy eating only. **Refer to a registered dietitian** for elimination diets, supplements, significant GI symptoms, any history of disordered eating, or if she's trying to conceive. Present the dietary approach as "may help, low risk, good for performance." Endometriosis diet research is limited.

## E1. Core Principles

| Principle | Target |
|---|---|
| Mediterranean-style base | Vegetables, legumes, whole grains, olive oil, fish |
| Protein | ~1.6 g/kg/day across 3–4 meals of 25–35 g (e.g., 65 kg ≈ 105 g) |
| Omega-3 | Oily fish 2–3×/week, plus walnuts, chia, flax |
| Fibre | 25–30 g/day, built up gradually. Reduce temporarily if bloating flares. |
| Plants | 5+ portions/day, including cruciferous veg and berries |
| Fat | Extra-virgin olive oil as the main fat |
| Fluids | ~2–2.5 L/day, plus ~500 ml per hour of exercise (more in summer heat) |

**Less often (not banned):** red meat (~1–2×/week), processed meat, ultra-processed foods, added sugar, and alcohol (avoid around flow and flare windows). Caffeine up to ~2–3 coffees a day, less if it affects pain or sleep. Rigid restriction adds stress, which is one of her flare triggers.

**Energy:** Maintenance throughout. **No calorie deficit during Phases 2–3.** High intensity combined with under-fuelling raises the risk of fatigue, cycle disruption, and flares. Any body-composition goal needs dietitian input and a deficit no larger than ~300 kcal/day.

## E2. Training-Day Fuelling

- **Strength, MetCon, interval, and test days:** higher carbohydrate. Have a carb snack 60–90 min before (banana, toast, oats) and a protein-plus-carb meal within ~2 h after.
- **Easy, G, and rest days:** moderate carbohydrate, protein at every meal.
- **Sessions over 60 min** (W9 and W11 Saturdays): carb snack beforehand, and bring water plus a banana or dates.
- **No fasted cardio.**
- **Weeks with 4–5 hard days** (W2–W4, W6–W9, W11): watch for downward weight drift or unusual fatigue. Either is a cue to add food.

## E3. Sample Training Day (~65 kg)

- **Breakfast:** Overnight oats with Greek yoghurt, chia, berries, walnuts (~30 g protein)
- **Lunch:** Quinoa or lentil salad with roast veg, greens, sardines or chicken, olive oil and lemon (~30 g)
- **Pre-training:** Banana with almonds, or toast with nut butter
- **Dinner:** Salmon, sweet potato, broccoli, tahini (~35 g)
- **Optional evening:** Kefir or yoghurt with ground flax (~10–15 g)

**Sunday batch cook:** grains, roast veg trays, lentil or bean soup, salmon or chicken portions, dressing jars.

## E4. Cycle and Flare Adjustments

- **Flow days:** iron-rich foods (red meat allowance, lentils, spinach, tofu, fortified cereal) paired with vitamin C, and tea or coffee kept away from these meals. Warm, easy meals. Magnesium-rich foods. Ginger tea and a heat pack.
- **Flare days:** don't skip meals; small, frequent meals work better. If she's bloated, temporarily switch to cooked veg, rice, oats, eggs, fish, and yoghurt, and cut back on raw cruciferous veg, beans, onion, and garlic. Avoid alcohol and reduce caffeine.
- **Luteal phase (7–10 days before flow):** allow the extra appetite with complex carbs and protein. Ease up on salt if she's bloated.
- **Before high-intensity weeks near restricted windows** (W6, W8): keep iron and hydration steady.

## E5. Supplements

Refer, don't prescribe. Omega-3, vitamin D, magnesium, and iron (if deficient) have some research behind them. She should discuss these with her GP, gynaecologist, or a dietitian, because some can interact with hormonal treatment. Low ferritin directly limits aerobic gains.

# PART F: Recovery, Monitoring, and Referral

## F1. Recovery

- 7–9 h sleep. If she averages under 7 h, prioritise sleep over adding load.
- 3–5 min of diaphragmatic breathing after every hard session, especially useful for a hypertonic pelvic floor.
- Stress management matters, since flares often track stress.

## F2. Daily Log

- Pelvic pain 0–10: before training, after training, and the next morning
- Fatigue, bloating, bowel and bladder symptoms, sleep, and resting HR
- Session details: top-set RPE, whether she braced on the exhale throughout, MetCon RPE, foot contacts and landing quality, cardio minutes, modality, and average HR
- Any leaking, heaviness, or breath-holding
- A rough meal photo log, plus alcohol, caffeine, and any suspected trigger foods
- Cycle day, and actual flow and flare dates (to update predictions)

**Review at 4–6 weeks.** If food patterns emerge, refer her to a dietitian (for example, for low-FODMAP) rather than having her self-restrict.

## F3. Back-Off Triggers

| Trigger | Action |
|---|---|
| Pain 2+ points higher the morning after a hard session | Ease off for the rest of the week |
| Two consecutive failed readiness checks | Rest of the week at G or Zone 2 |
| Resting HR up 5–7+ bpm for 2+ days (outside luteal phase) | Replace HIIT with Zone 2 |
| Easy pace feels hard for more than a week | Reduce load and check ferritin |
| Pelvic symptoms on landing | Regress plyos one level |
| Unplanned flare | G sessions, then restart at the previous week's loads once settled |

## F4. Refer Promptly

- **Gynaecologist or physio:** pain that's new or different in character, pain that persists after lifting, bleeding outside expected flow, any leaking or heaviness with impact or load.
- **GP:** unusual breathlessness, chest symptoms, dizziness, or signs of anaemia.
- **GP or dietitian:** rapid weight loss, fear of foods, increasingly restrictive eating, persistent GI symptoms (including blood), or missed or significantly changed periods.

# Complete 12-Week Programme: 34F, Stage III Endometriosis

**Start:** Monday 1 June 2026 · **End:** Sunday 23 August 2026

This version includes every adjustment we made: the base plan, the nutrition plan, the aerobic base cardio, the higher-intensity Phase 2, the MetCon day, the plyometric day, and end-of-block e1RM testing. Where later changes replaced earlier ones, only the final version appears.

---

# PART A: Ground Rules

## A1. Clearance (before Week 1)

- **Gynaecologist sign-off.** Stage III often involves adhesions and endometriomas.
- **Pelvic floor physio assessment.** She needs clearance for **heavier loading** before Phase 2 and for **impact** before any jumping (from Week 5). Without impact clearance, she repeats the Phase 1 landing-prep drills and uses med-ball power work instead of jumps.
- **Bloods via her GP:** ferritin, vitamin D, B12.

## A2. Projected Restricted Days

These are based on her last period (4 May 2026), a 27-day cycle, and 4 flow days. **Confirm her dates every week.** Check especially in Week 11, because the e1RM test depends on it.

| Type | Dates | Programme week |
|---|---|---|
| Flow 1 | Mon 1 – Wed 3 Jun (began Sun 31 May) | W1 |
| Flow 2 | Sat 27 – Tue 30 Jun | W4–W5 |
| Flare 1 | Fri 10 – Mon 13 Jul | W6–W7 |
| Flow 3 | Fri 24 – Mon 27 Jul | W8–W9 |
| Flare 2 | Tue 4 – Fri 7 Aug | W10 |
| Flow 4 | Thu 20 – Sun 23 Aug | W12 |

## A3. Restriction Rules

| Rule | Applies to |
|---|---|
| **No HIIT, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping** | Every flow and flare day. Use the Gentle Session (G) or rest. |
| **No MetCon or plyos the day before** a flow or flare day | All phases |
| **No MetCon or plyos in the first session back** after flow or a flare | All phases |
| **Strength RPE capped at 7.5 the day before** a flow or flare day | Phases 2–3 |
| **Max 2 HIIT-type sessions per week** (MetCon + intervals). Plyos don't count toward this cap. | All phases |
| **Max 1 impact (plyo) session per week** | All phases |
| **About 80%+ of cardio time is easy** | All phases |
| **Exhale-on-effort bracing on every day.** No breath-held lifts. | All phases |
| **No training to failure.** Leave 1–2 reps in reserve on main lifts. | All phases |
| **Pain overrides the plan.** Unplanned pain means G or rest that day. | Always |

**Cycle drift:** If her dates shift, re-apply every rule above to the new dates. Move or cancel any MetCon, plyo session, heavy strength day, or test that now lands on a restricted day, the day before one, or the first session after one.

## A4. Readiness Check (before every hard session)

Hard sessions are Strength A/B, MetCon, intervals, plyos, and tests.

| Check | Go | Downgrade |
|---|---|---|
| Pelvic pain (0–10) | ≤ 3 | 4–5: RPE 7 max, no MetCon, intervals, or plyos. 6+: G session. |
| Sleep | Normal | Under 6 h: drop one set per main lift, skip plyos |
| Resting HR | Within ~5 bpm of normal | Up 5–7+ bpm for 2+ days (outside luteal phase): Zone 2 instead of HIIT |
| Early flare signs | None | Treat the day as restricted |

**Order to drop elements when she's run-down:** plyos first, then MetCon, then intervals. Keep strength and Zone 2 where possible.

---

# PART B: Session Library

## B1. Gentle Session (G), 20–40 min, for restricted days

- 10–20 min easy walk, elliptical, or recumbent bike at RPE 3–4 (low-impact only)
- 5 min diaphragmatic breathing in supported child's pose or 90/90
- Cat-cow, open book, supported hip-flexor stretch, figure-4, happy baby: 2 × 45 s each
- Optional, exhaling on effort: glute bridge 2×12, banded row 2×15, dead bug 2×8/side
- Heat pack afterwards if helpful

## B2. Easy Cardio (Zone 2)

- **Intensity:** full sentences possible (talk test overrules everything else), RPE 3–4, roughly 112–130 bpm. Heart rate runs higher in the luteal phase and on bad days. When that happens, slow down to keep the same effort.
- **Modalities:** incline walk, elliptical, rower, swim, outdoor walk or hike. Cycle only if saddle pressure is comfortable; otherwise use a recumbent bike or a cut-out saddle. Run only on unrestricted days, if her physio has cleared it and it's symptom-free.
- **Progression:** no more than 10–15% more easy minutes per week. Never catch up missed minutes.

## B3. Strength Sessions

**Phase 1 (W1–W4): RPE 6–7, 3+ reps in reserve, 60–90 s rest**

| Strength A | Strength B |
|---|---|
| Goblet squat 3×10 | DB bench or incline press 3×10 |
| DB Romanian deadlift 3×10 | 1-arm row 3×10/side |
| Split squat 3×8/side | Lat pulldown 3×10 |
| Glute bridge 3×12 | KB deadlift 3×10 |
| Pallof press 3×10/side | Side plank 3×20 s/side |

**Phase 2 (W5–W8): RPE 8–8.5, supersets, 1–2 reps in reserve**

| Strength A | Rest | Strength B | Rest |
|---|---|---|---|
| Back or safety-bar squat: top set + 3 back-off sets | 2.5–3 min | Bench press: top set + 3 back-off sets | 2.5–3 min |
| RDL 3×6–8 | 2 min | Trap-bar deadlift 3×5–6 | 2.5 min |
| **SS:** reverse lunge 3×8/side + low box step-down 3×8/side | 90 s | **SS:** chest-supported row 4×8 + half-kneeling landmine press 3×8/side | 90 s |
| Hip thrust 3×8, 2 s pause | 90 s | Assisted pull-up 3×6–8 (less assistance weekly) | 90 s |
| Suitcase carry 3×30 m/side | 60 s | Pallof press, 3 s hold, 3×8/side | 45 s |

| Week | Top set | Back-off |
|---|---|---|
| W5 | 1×8 @ RPE 7 | 3×8 @ −5% |
| W6 | 1×6 @ RPE 8 (Thu capped at 7.5) | 3×6–8 @ −10% |
| W7 | 1×6 @ RPE 8 (Tue re-entry at RPE 7) | 3×6 @ −10% |
| W8 | 1×5 @ RPE 8.5 (Thu capped at 7.5) | 3×5 @ −10% |

**Load increases:** If she hits the target RPE with clean exhaled bracing, add 2.5–5 kg on lower-body lifts and 1–2.5 kg on upper-body lifts the next week. Hold the load if she breath-holds, feels pelvic heaviness, leaks, or has pain.

**Phase 3 (W9–W12): 4–6 reps, stop at RPE 8, controlled exhale bracing only**

| Strength A | Strength B |
|---|---|
| Squat 4×5 | Bench press 4×5 |
| RDL 4×6 | Weighted or assisted pull-up 4×5 |
| Bulgarian split squat 3×6/side | Barbell row 4×6 |
| Hip thrust 4×8 | Trap-bar deadlift 4×5 |
| Farmer carry 4×30 m | Copenhagen plank 3×15 s/side |

| Week | Target |
|---|---|
| W9 | RPE 7.5 (post-flow re-entry on Tue) |
| W10 | Mon only, RPE cap 7.5 (day before flare) |
| W11 | RPE 8 (RPE 7 on Mon if Saturday's post-flare walk didn't feel normal) |
| W12 | e1RM tests (B8) |

## B4. Interval Sessions (Friday unless moved)

Always include a 10 min warm-up and a 5–10 min cool-down. Use the rower, elliptical, or bike (bike only if the saddle is comfortable). **No plyos attached to intervals** except in W5.

| Phase | Session |
|---|---|
| Phase 1 | Tempo: 6 × 1 min @ RPE 7, 2 min easy |
| Phase 2 | W5: 8 × 30 s @ RPE 8–9 / 90 s easy · W7: 6 × 2 min @ RPE 8–9 / 90 s easy + 4 × 20 s sprints |
| Phase 3 | 10 × 40 s hard / 80 s easy |

## B5. MetCon

**Allowed:** rower, ski erg, air bike or elliptical, sled push or drag, KB swing (moderate), DB step-up, battle ropes, med ball chest pass, light DB push press, farmer carry, TRX or DB row.

**Excluded:** burpees, box jumps, jump squats, double-unders, wall balls, any jumping, heavy barbell cycling, sit-ups and crunches, and anything she needs to breath-hold to finish.

**Loads:** about 40–60% of her 10-rep load. Pace provides the difficulty. Always include a 10 min warm-up, a 5 min cool-down, and 3–5 min of diaphragmatic breathing. Stop immediately with any leaking, heaviness, or pain.

| Session | Week / date | Prescription | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intro Circuit | W2 · Tue 9 Jun | 3 rounds, 40 s on / 20 s off: row → light KB deadlift → DB step-up → ropes. 60 s between rounds. (~12 min) | 6–7 |
| Intro Circuit + | W3 · Tue 16 Jun | 4 rounds of the same. KB deadlift becomes a light swing if her hinge is solid. (~16 min) | 6–7 |
| Light Flush | W4 · Tue 23 Jun | 2 rounds of W3 (~8 min). Skip if she's run-down. | 6 |
| EMOM 16 | W6 · Tue 7 Jul | 12 cal row → 10 KB swings → 20 m sled push → 30 s ropes, ×4 rounds | 8 |
| Short and Sharp | W8 · Tue 21 Jul | 3 rounds, 30 s hard / 30 s easy: ski erg → light DB push press → air bike → farmer carry. 90 s between rounds. (~12 min) | 8 |
| AMRAP 2 × 8 | W9 · Fri 31 Jul | 2 × 8 min AMRAP, 3 min easy between: 10 cal row, 10 KB swings, 20 m sled push, 8/side DB step-ups | 8–8.5 |
| Peak EMOM 20 | W11 · Tue 11 Aug | 14 cal row → 12 KB swings → 20 m heavy sled push → 10/side DB step-ups → 30 s ropes, ×4 rounds | 8–8.5 |

**Alternative:** If aerobic power is a higher priority than metabolic conditioning, run the Phase 2 intervals instead of MetCon in W6 and W8, and Phase 3 intervals instead of MetCon in W9.

## B6. Plyometrics (Wednesday, before Zone 2)

**Never used:** depth or drop jumps, boxes above ~30 cm, jumping down (she steps down), tuck jumps, maximal bounding, burpees.

**Structure:** 8 min warm-up (5 min easy cardio, leg swings, ankle rocks, glute bridge ×10, 3 min breathing with gentle pelvic floor engage/relax), then the plyo block (8–12 min), then straight into Zone 2. Rest 60–90 s between sets. Exhale on take-off and landing.

| W2 | Wed 10 Jun | **Landing prep (no jumps):** snap-down 3×5 · fast-up calf raise 2×12 · lateral step-and-stick 2×5/side · med ball chest pass 2×6 | 0 |

- **Refer to her physio** after any leaking or heaviness, even once.

## B7. Aerobic Test (fixed effort)

10 min easy, then **20 min at ~125 bpm** (or the top of her talk-test zone) on the same machine each time. Record distance or average watts, plus her cycle day.

- **Baseline:** Sat 6 Jun
- **Retest:** Tue 18 Aug

More output at the same heart rate means her base has improved. Interpret small differences cautiously if the two tests fall in different cycle phases.

## B8. Estimated 1RM Test (W12)

**No true 1RM this block.** A max single requires a breath-held Valsalva, which conflicts with the exhale-bracing rule. The only safe test window before flow is also very narrow.

- **Warm-up:** bar ×10, ~50% ×5, ~70% ×3, ~85% ×1, then rest 3–4 min.
- **Test set:** 3–5 reps at RPE 8–9 with exhale bracing. If the set is clean and well under RPE 8, she may take one more set at +2.5–5 kg. Maximum two test sets per lift.
- **Formula:** e1RM = load × (1 + reps ÷ 30). For example, 60 kg × 4 ≈ 68 kg.
- **Set is void** if she breath-holds, her form breaks, or she has any pelvic symptom. Use the last clean set instead.
- **Trap-bar deadlift:** calculate from W11 Thursday's heaviest clean set. Don't test it in W12.
- **Pull-up:** use max reps at her current assistance, or a weighted 5RM, in W11.
- **Test only if:** she passes the readiness check, the W10 flare has settled, W11 went normally, and her cycle dates are confirmed. Otherwise, use her W11 working sets as end-of-block numbers.

# PART E: Nutrition

**Scope:** General healthy eating only. **Refer to a registered dietitian** for elimination diets, supplements, significant GI symptoms, any history of disordered eating, or if she's trying to conceive. Present the dietary approach as "may help, low risk, good for performance." Endometriosis diet research is limited.

## E1. Core Principles

| Principle | Target |
|---|---|
| Mediterranean-style base | Vegetables, legumes, whole grains, olive oil, fish |
| Protein | ~1.6 g/kg/day across 3–4 meals of 25–35 g (e.g., 65 kg ≈ 105 g) |
| Omega-3 | Oily fish 2–3×/week, plus walnuts, chia, flax |
| Fibre | 25–30 g/day, built up gradually. Reduce temporarily if bloating flares. |
| Plants | 5+ portions/day, including cruciferous veg and berries |
| Fat | Extra-virgin olive oil as the main fat |
| Fluids | ~2–2.5 L/day, plus ~500 ml per hour of exercise (more in summer heat) |

**Less often (not banned):** red meat (~1–2×/week), processed meat, ultra-processed foods, added sugar, and alcohol (avoid around flow and flare windows). Caffeine up to ~2–3 coffees a day, less if it affects pain or sleep. Rigid restriction adds stress, which is one of her flare triggers.

**Energy:** Maintenance throughout. **No calorie deficit during Phases 2–3.** High intensity combined with under-fuelling raises the risk of fatigue, cycle disruption, and flares. Any body-composition goal needs dietitian input and a deficit no larger than ~300 kcal/day.

## E2. Training-Day Fuelling

- **Strength, MetCon, interval, and test days:** higher carbohydrate. Have a carb snack 60–90 min before (banana, toast, oats) and a protein-plus-carb meal within ~2 h after.
- **Easy, G, and rest days:** moderate carbohydrate, protein at every meal.
- **Sessions over 60 min** (W9 and W11 Saturdays): carb snack beforehand, and bring water plus a banana or dates.
- **No fasted cardio.**
- **Weeks with 4–5 hard days** (W2–W4, W6–W9, W11): watch for downward weight drift or unusual fatigue. Either is a cue to add food.

## E3. Sample Training Day (~65 kg)

- **Breakfast:** Overnight oats with Greek yoghurt, chia, berries, walnuts (~30 g protein)
- **Lunch:** Quinoa or lentil salad with roast veg, greens, sardines or chicken, olive oil and lemon (~30 g)
- **Pre-training:** Banana with almonds, or toast with nut butter
- **Dinner:** Salmon, sweet potato, broccoli, tahini (~35 g)
- **Optional evening:** Kefir or yoghurt with ground flax (~10–15 g)

**Sunday batch cook:** grains, roast veg trays, lentil or bean soup, salmon or chicken portions, dressing jars.

## E4. Cycle and Flare Adjustments

- **Flow days:** iron-rich foods (red meat allowance, lentils, spinach, tofu, fortified cereal) paired with vitamin C, and tea or coffee kept away from these meals. Warm, easy meals. Magnesium-rich foods. Ginger tea and a heat pack.
- **Flare days:** don't skip meals; small, frequent meals work better. If she's bloated, temporarily switch to cooked veg, rice, oats, eggs, fish, and yoghurt, and cut back on raw cruciferous veg, beans, onion, and garlic. Avoid alcohol and reduce caffeine.
- **Luteal phase (7–10 days before flow):** allow the extra appetite with complex carbs and protein. Ease up on salt if she's bloated.
- **Before high-intensity weeks near restricted windows** (W6, W8): keep iron and hydration steady.

## E5. Supplements

Refer, don't prescribe. Omega-3, vitamin D, magnesium, and iron (if deficient) have some research behind them. She should discuss these with her GP, gynaecologist, or a dietitian, because some can interact with hormonal treatment. Low ferritin directly limits aerobic gains.

---

# PART F: Recovery, Monitoring, and Referral

## F1. Recovery

- 7–9 h sleep. If she averages under 7 h, prioritise sleep over adding load.
- 3–5 min of diaphragmatic breathing after every hard session, especially useful for a hypertonic pelvic floor.
- Stress management matters, since flares often track stress.

## F2. Daily Log

- Pelvic pain 0–10: before training, after training, and the next morning
- Fatigue, bloating, bowel and bladder symptoms, sleep, and resting HR
- Session details: top-set RPE, whether she braced on the exhale throughout, MetCon RPE, foot contacts and landing quality, cardio minutes, modality, and average HR
- Any leaking, heaviness, or breath-holding
- A rough meal photo log, plus alcohol, caffeine, and any suspected trigger foods
- Cycle day, and actual flow and flare dates (to update predictions)

**Review at 4–6 weeks.** If food patterns emerge, refer her to a dietitian (for example, for low-FODMAP) rather than having her self-restrict.

## F3. Back-Off Triggers

| Trigger | Action |
|---|---|
| Pain 2+ points higher the morning after a hard session | Ease off for the rest of the week |
| Two consecutive failed readiness checks | Rest of the week at G or Zone 2 |
| Resting HR up 5–7+ bpm for 2+ days (outside luteal phase) | Replace HIIT with Zone 2 |
| Easy pace feels hard for more than a week | Reduce load and check ferritin |
| Pelvic symptoms on landing | Regress plyos one level |
| Unplanned flare | G sessions, then restart at the previous week's loads once settled |
